title: Tokyo says some QUO Card Pay codes from its Akachan First childcare programme cannot be used; contractor had reported unauthorized access
date_note: Date of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government press release; the page gives no earlier day for the announcement.
summary: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government said some QUO Card Pay codes obtained by exchanging points in its Akachan First childcare programme cannot be used and some balances have dropped. It says the cause is not from the QUO Card Pay issuer's system. The contractor, Linbell, announced unauthorized access earlier; Tokyo does not state whether the two are related. No leak of personal information has been confirmed.
plain: Some gift-card codes that Tokyo gave to new parents cannot be used or have lost value. Tokyo says no leak of personal information is confirmed and will have codes reissued.
exec: A Tokyo government benefit was disrupted, and the contractor behind it had reported unauthorized access; Tokyo has not said the two are related.
action: Tokyo advises affected holders to wait for an email from the contractor to their registered address with reissued codes, and to contact the Akachan First call center with questions.

validation.note: Tokyo Metropolitan Government's own press release and ITmedia NEWS (independent publisher) both state the QUO Card Pay problem and the closure of the exchange site.
